textContent: Full Day Kolkata City Tour: Mother House, Kumartuli & Flower Market  Tour Duration 7 to 8 hours (Flexible)  Easy Pickup Free hotel pickup & drop.  Language English  Tour Assistance Available free with every tour. Full Day Kolkata City Tour - Highlights This Full Day Kolkata City Tour is private and guided, usually running 7–8 hours with flexible start times between 08:00 AM and 12:00 PM. Visit Mullick Ghat Flower Market with frames of the Howrah Bridge and riverside bustle under Asia’s most atmospheric wholesale flower stretch. Visit the serene Mother House to understand Kolkata’s living legacy of service and contemplation. Wander Kumartuli’s artisan lanes to witness clay idols that shape the soul of Durga Puja and Bengal’s cultural calendar. College Street (Boi Para) browsing and Indian Coffee House adda for bookish nostalgia, rare finds, and classic café lore. Heritage drive-by with postcard stops: Victoria Memorial, Maidan, BBD Bagh facades, and river-view corridors. In this Kolkata City Tour Kolkata comes alive in a single, thoughtfully curated day that spans color-drenched markets, quiet moments of reflection, and storied boulevards framed by grand colonial architecture and riverside life along the Hooghly. This Private Guided Tour in Kolkata is ideal for visitors who want signature stops—Mullick Ghat Flower Market, Mother House, and Kumartuli—balanced with a panoramic heritage loop past landmarks like Victoria Memorial, Maidan, and BBD Bagh. Expect an early start to catch the markets at their most atmospheric in this Calcutta City Tour, a mid-morning shift to Kolkata’s spiritual heart, and an afternoon of artisan storytelling, bookish browsing, and café nostalgia before a golden-hour drive through the city’s grand vistas. With flexible pacing, travelers can linger where interests run deepest, from photography and faith history to crafts, books, and riverside frames. About the Tour: Full Day Calcutta City Tour Full Day Calcutta City Tour “in a day” arc connects the city’s essential trio—market, mission, and makers—while linking the dots with a river-hugging bridge view and a colonial skyline that still shapes the urban imagination. This plan suits first-time visitors aiming for must-sees as well as culture-lovers returning to go deeper in artisan quarters and historic institutions. Who it’s for: Travelers seeking a private, customizable day with cultural depth, light walking, and curated stories spanning faith, craft, and heritage. Start points: Our Tour Expert / Guide will pick up guests from any Hotel or Guest House within Kolkata city limits or from the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International (NSCBI) Airport. After completing the tour, guests will be dropped back at the same location — ensuring a smooth, comfortable, and convenient experience throughout in this Private Calcutta City Tour. Transit Travelers: Importantly, this tour is also ideal for transit travelers. We offer convenient Airport pickup between 7:30 AM and 12:30 PM and ensure a timely drop-off aligned with your Flight Schedule—making it possible to explore Kolkata comfortably even on a short layover. We’re here to make your travel planning as smooth and enjoyable as possible. What time should this tour start? Our tours usually begin at 9:00 AM, which we find to be the most comfortable time for covering the itinerary smoothly. However, we understand that every traveler has different plans and preferences. We are happy to offer flexibility, and the tour can be scheduled to start anytime between 8:00 AM and 12:00 PM, as per your convenience. Please let us know your preferred start time in advance so that we can make the necessary arrangements. Are there specific visiting hours for Mother House? Yes, commonly 8am–12pm and 3pm–6pm, closed Thursdays; always check the latest schedule before visiting. Is photography allowed everywhere? Yes! This tour is exceptionally rich in photographic opportunities, from architectural marvels and colorful markets to traditional craftsmen and spiritual ceremonies. Your guide will identify the best photography spots and explain cultural context for meaningful images. Please be respectful at religious sites and follow posted rules or staff guidance. How much walking is involved? Light to moderate walking in markets and lanes amd by-lanes; if you can walk little more, then you can see more life. Is this tour suitable for families and seniors? Yes, with flexible pacing, rest stops, and route adjustments tailored to comfort and interests. What should travelers wear? Modest, comfortable clothing for religious sites; breathable fabrics, sun protection, and closed shoes for uneven lanes. Can this be customized for interests like photography or food? Yes—timing, stops, and dwell time can be prioritized for photography, bookstores, cafés, or heritage interiors. Are entry fees included? Entry fees vary by site and can be included or paid on the spot depending on booking configuration and availability. Posted on Tripadvisor Inspire59089999388 15 April 2026 Verified A Truly Enriching Journey to the Hidden Gems of Bishnupur We recently had the pleasure of experiencing the Hidden Treasures of Bishnupur – Private Day Tour from Kolkata with Kolkata Trips, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable cultural excursions I’ve taken in West Bengal. The journey begins early in the morning with a comfortable pick-up from Kolkata. Although the drive to Bishnupur takes around 3.5 to 4 hours each way, the scenic countryside—lush green paddy fields, rustic villages, and peaceful rural landscapes—makes the journey quite enjoyable and refreshing. What truly sets this tour apart is the depth of cultural immersion. Bishnupur is a treasure trove of heritage, famous for its stunning terracotta temples built during the Malla dynasty. Exploring iconic sites like Ras Mancha, Shyam Rai Temple, Jor Bangla Temple, and Madanmohan Temple was an absolute delight. The intricate terracotta carvings depicting mythological stories are simply breathtaking and offer a fascinating glimpse into Bengal’s rich artistic legacy. A special mention must go to the guide, whose knowledge and storytelling brought each monument to life. The historical context, architectural details, and cultural anecdotes added immense value to the experience. The tour is well-paced, allowing ample time at each site without feeling rushed, and the private setup ensures a very personalized and flexible experience. Another highlight was the opportunity to witness local craftsmanship, especially the famous Baluchari silk weaving. It added a unique dimension to the tour, connecting history with living traditions. Yes, it is a long day (approximately 12 hours), but every moment feels worthwhile. The comfort of an air-conditioned vehicle, seamless planning, and attentive service make the experience smooth and enjoyable throughout. Overall, this tour is perfect for anyone interested in history, architecture, and authentic cultural experiences. If you’re looking to explore beyond Kolkata and discover a lesser-known yet incredibly rich heritage destination, Bishnupur is a must-visit—and Kolkata Trips does a fantastic job curating this journey.
